newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine unsecured loans business seen growing.
newsitem.headline: Philippine unsecured loans business seen growing.

text.p: The Philippine banking industry is likely to see the introduction of new products offering unsecured personal credit, a senior Citibank official said.

"I believe (this) will happen in this market going forward. There will appear to be a new set of products in the banking sector where customers can go and take unsecured credit," Harpal Dugal, vice president and business manager for Citibank's credit card division in the Philippines, said in an interview on Monday.
Dugal was responding to questions about the surge in the credit cards business in the Philippines which is seen growing by between 30 and 40 percent annually.
Total spending through credit cards in the Philippines is around 45 billion to 50 billion pesos annually compared to around 16 billion to 18 billion pesos in 1993.
Citibank Philippines, a unit of Citicorp, dominates the country's credit cards business.
Dugal attributed the surge in business to the improving Philippine economy and pointed out the industry started from a low base about three years ago.
The scarcity of unsecured credit was also an important factor, he said.
"You can borrow to buy a car, a house, but the personal loan (sector) has been completely dominated by the unofficial sector till 1992/93, with pawnshops and the like," he said.

"Unofficial lenders, their rates are 50 or 60 percent and banks for some reason are not offering consumer unsecured credit at rates of 25 and 35 percent, which I believe will happen in this market going forward, he said.
"In the meantime credit cards are offering rates between 33 and 45 percent."
Dugal declined to give profit figures for Citibank Philippines but industry analysts said the bank's profits from this division had risen 10-fold in the last three years.
